episodes.title: In 1956, the future kitchen looked like this
episodes.headline:
THE FUTURE KITCHEN
ACCORDING TO 1956

beats.text: In 1956, the kitchen of tomorrow came with a recipe screen. The touchscreen? Not included.
In this General Motors promotional fantasy, you insert a card, see the dish, and let the push-button spectacle begin.
The mixer drops from a cabinet. The refrigerator puts its contents on a rotating display.
Even the oven opens like a tiny spaceship. Subtle? Absolutely not.
The promise wasn't just dinner. It was freedom from housework, with time left over for fun.
They imagined a kitchen that performed for you. Somehow, we still ended up arguing about who loads the dishwasher.

episodes.title: In 1956, tomorrow's commute looked like science fiction
episodes.headline:
YOUR FUTURE COMMUTE
ACCORDING TO 1956

beats.text: This is what a 1956 promotional film imagined your future commute would look like. Apparently, traffic wasn't invited.
Design for Dreaming presents General Motors dream cars like stars on a fashion runway.
The shapes are theatrical. The reveal is a performance. Getting somewhere is only half the fantasy.
Before the final drive, the couple contacts a control tower. Even a road trip gets the airport treatment.
Then we enter a miniature city of tomorrow, with sweeping roads and gleaming buildings.
It's a sales pitch, not a forecast. But there's one prediction I still want: a commute that feels like the ending of a musical.
